description: NOAA Workshop Series: Habitat Conservation in a Changing Climate is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); NOAA Fisheries Office of Habitat Conservation. In 2010, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) hosted a series of meetings to create tools and strategies to help natural resource managers and decision makers prepare for changes in climate. These meetings focused on selective habitat conservation as a tool for climate change adaptation. Coverage: the United States (2010). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
